generatedProse.concept-context: In sport, the three strands run together across training, competition and placement. You own an experience, such as a coaching session or your own performance, carry it through the cycle so the reflection is critical, then write it up for a training log or portfolio. Done after each one, with a change carried into the next session, the rounds build your practice over the season.
generatedProse.worked-example: Two sport students get the same feedback on an early coaching assessment. One moves to the next session and keeps making the same call under pressure. The other owns it, runs the session through the cycle, writes an evaluation against coaching standards, and changes how he sets up the drill. Over the season his coaching improves, because the three strands ran as one practice.
generatedProse.summary: In sport, reflective practice matters most when the three strands run as one. You own each session or performance, work it through the cycle, and write an evaluation that justifies a change. It is the repeated practice, not any single reflection, that develops you as a practitioner.

check.body: A newly qualified practitioner owns a difficult episode, runs it through the cycle to reach a change, writes it up as an evaluation, and applies the change next time. What does this show?

items.text: Their next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following programme improved.
Nothing; feedback comes at the end, so it cannot affect anything that follows.
Only the mark on the first programme, which cannot now change.
The deadline for the next programme.

feedback.correct: That's right. Using the feedback fed back into the next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following programme improved: that is the cycle working.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what the student changed before the next programme, not the old mark or the deadline.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Using the feedback fed back into the student's next round of learning and preparation, which is why the next programme improved. The old mark cannot change and the deadline is not part of the cycle; feedback is not the end, it feeds the next turn.

_items.text: That the three strands work as one practice: the stance, the cycle and the writing together produced a change that improved the next experience.
_items.feedback: Yes. The whole loop ran: own it, reflect critically, write the evaluation, carry the change forward.

_items.text: That the practitioner simply described the episode in more detail than before.
_items.feedback: Describing is only the start. Here the practitioner evaluated and changed, which is the practice.

_items.text: That writing the reflection down was the only part that mattered.
_items.feedback: The writing records the work, but the stance and the cycle did the reflecting first.

_items.text: That the episode would now never happen again.
_items.feedback: Reflection does not guarantee that. It changes how you act and keep developing.
